primitives.name: Causal Validation Verdict
primitives.verbatim_quote: Logic of scientific discovery: *failing to falsify* the model on probes increases trust in the target estimate; a failed probe is evidence something (graph, estimation, or the expectations themselves) is wrong.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\theta': 'minimum acceptable hit rate threshold (dimensionless)', '\\text{Verdict}': 'validation outcome (binary: Accept/Reject)'}
primitives.assumptions: A valid causal model must produce consistent predictions across all relevant non-target effects under domain constraints.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If any probe fails consistently across multiple runs, it suggests either incorrect domain knowledge, flawed estimation procedure, or erroneous causal graph.

layer2.mapping: Validation verdict synthesizes empirical feedback from probe outcomes into a decision rule for model acceptability.
layer2.telemetry: Binary classification of model validity based on probe performance

primitives.name: Probe Failure Diagnosis
primitives.verbatim_quote: Equations & assumptions - Probe hit: |τ̂_probe - τ_probe| ≤ ε_probe counts as success.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\text{Failure Set}': 'set of indices for failed probes (dimensionless)', '\\hat{\\tau}_i': 'estimated effect of probe i (same units as \\tau_i)', '\\tau_i': 'true effect of probe i (same units as \\hat{\\tau}_i)', '\\varepsilon_{\\text{probe}}': 'tolerance threshold for probe acceptance (same units as \\tau_i)'}
primitives.assumptions: Failed probes can be clustered to isolate components of the causal graph responsible for discrepancies.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High cardinality failure sets suggest systemic issues in estimation or graph learning rather than isolated errors.

layer2.mapping: Failure diagnosis enables targeted debugging by identifying subsets of probes that fail together, indicating localized structural or parametric errors.
layer2.telemetry: Set of failed probe indices used for clustering and localization of causal model defects

reasoning_traces.think:
Quantitative probing operates on the principle that a well-specified causal model should make accurate predictions about non-target effects derived from domain knowledge. This approach leverages the fact that causal graphs encode conditional independencies that constrain effect estimates. By formulating falsifiable expectations for these non-target effects, one can compute a hit rate—defined as the proportion of such expectations satisfied within a tolerance ε_probe. If the hit rate exceeds a predefined threshold θ, the model is accepted; otherwise, it is rejected. This process introduces a form of empirical validation akin to hypothesis testing but applied to entire causal structures rather than individual parameters. The key insight is that a model’s ability to predict non-target effects reflects its internal consistency and fidelity to the underlying causal mechanism. When probes fail, they provide diagnostic information that allows refinement of either the causal graph, the estimation procedure, or even the initial domain assumptions. Thus, the framework supports iterative improvement of causal models through structured experimentation and feedback loops.
